common_name: Nana Lutea Hinoki Cypress (Dwarf Golden Hinoki Falsecypress)

planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring so roots establish before summer heat, siting where the golden foliage gets some shelter from harsh afternoon sun.

directions: Nana Lutea is a slow-growing, conical dwarf selection of Hinoki cypress prized for its bright, buttery-gold new growth on flattened, fan-like sprays that deepen slightly to chartreuse-green with age. It colors best with a half-day of sun but can scorch in intense afternoon exposure in hot climates, so light shade during the hottest part of the day helps preserve the gold tone. Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and avoid heavy clay or standing water, which quickly leads to root problems. Needs little pruning beyond removing occasional dead interior growth, and its dense, compact habit suits rock gardens, foundation plantings, and container culture for many years before it outgrows a small space.

common_name: Fernspray Gold Hinoki Cypress (Golden Fern-Sprayed Falsecypress)

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil, choosing a site with morning sun and afternoon relief in hot regions to keep the gold foliage from bleaching.

directions: Fernspray Gold produces distinctive drooping, fern-like sprays of rich golden-yellow foliage on a broadly pyramidal, medium-sized shrub, giving it a softer, more graceful texture than most golden conifers. It grows faster than many Hinoki cultivars and can eventually reach small-tree size, so give it room to develop its cascading branch tips without crowding. Best gold color develops with several hours of direct sun, though some afternoon shade prevents scorch in climates with intense summer heat. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and avoid drought stress, which dulls the foliage color and can cause browning at the branch tips.

common_name: Kosteri Hinoki Cypress (Dwarf Irregular Cushion Falsecypress)

planting.note: Transplant in spring into well-drained soil and site in full sun to part shade, allowing space for its irregular, spreading mound habit.

directions: Kosteri is an old, dwarf Hinoki cypress cultivar with an irregular, cushion-like, spreading habit and dense, twisted sprays of dark green foliage that take on bronzy-purple tones in cold winter weather. Its slow growth and quirky, sculptural form make it a favorite for rock gardens, troughs, and bonsai-style specimen planting. Grow in moist but well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun for the most compact habit, though it tolerates part shade with slightly looser growth. Little pruning is required; occasional removal of dead interior twigs keeps the plant tidy, and winter protection from drying wind helps prevent foliage burn in the coldest zones.

planting.note: Plant in spring in moist, well-drained soil with shelter from harsh winter wind and reflected summer heat, which both stress this cultivar.

directions: Boulevard is a popular, densely pyramidal Sawara cypress cultivar with soft, silvery-blue, moss-like juvenile foliage that stays soft to the touch year-round, turning slightly plum-tinged in cold winters. It grows at a moderate pace into a broad cone shape and works well as a specimen, screen, or foundation anchor where its striking color can stand out against green plantings. Site in a spot with protection from strong winter wind and intense summer sun in hot climates, since both can brown or scorch the delicate foliage; part shade in the afternoon helps preserve color and vigor. Plant in evenly moist, well-drained soil and avoid letting it dry out, as this cultivar is less drought-tolerant than many other false cypress selections.

common_name: Little Giant Arborvitae (Dwarf Rounded Globe Arborvitae)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in full sun in well-drained soil; this true dwarf needs little more than an occasional deep watering to establish.

directions: Little Giant is a compact, globe-shaped dwarf arborvitae that holds a naturally tidy, rounded form without shearing, growing only a couple of inches per year to stay well under three feet for decades. Its dense, bright green, fan-like foliage keeps good color through winter with only slight bronzing in the coldest exposures. Plant in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained soil; it tolerates a range of soil types but performs poorly in wet, poorly drained sites. Use it as a low foundation accent, rock garden specimen, or repeated element in a formal border, and protect it from heavy wet snow load, which can splay the dense branching.

common_name: Mr. Bowling Ball Arborvitae (Miniature Soft-Textured Globe Arborvitae)

planting.note: Set out in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; this miniature globe needs minimal care once established and never needs shearing to hold its shape.

directions: Mr. Bowling Ball is a true miniature arborvitae forming a naturally neat, perfectly round sphere of soft, feathery, thread-like green foliage that turns a warm plum-brown in winter before greening back up in spring. Its extremely slow growth and small mature size make it one of the most popular dwarf conifers for small-space landscapes, edging, and container plantings. Plant in full sun in moist, well-drained soil for the densest habit and best winter color, since too much shade causes looser, more open growth. It requires no pruning to maintain its globe form and is generally trouble-free, though good drainage is essential to avoid root rot in wet soils.
